calls.head: Two of the league’s heaviest-hitting teams
calls.body: The Flyers and the Senators are both among the league’s heaviest hitters, even after adjusting for each arena’s scorer. Keep your head up.
calls.call: The two teams’ combined hit score reaches their usual 116.
calls.nums: Hit score (100 is league average): Philadelphia 111 (6th), Ottawa 122 (2nd)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The two teams’ combined hit score was 110, against their usual 116 (100 is league average, after adjusting for the arena’s scorer).

calls.head: Bring a pillow
calls.body: Philadelphia plays some of the league’s slowest games, and so does Ottawa. We think this one is even quieter than either team’s usual.
calls.call: The game runs at fewer than 77.5 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, slower than either team’s usual.
calls.nums: Pace (shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams): Philadelphia 31st (77.5), Ottawa 25th (79.3)
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 77.1 shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the slower team’s usual 77.5 and a league average of 81.5.

calls.head: The Senators lock it down; the Flyers don’t
calls.body: The Senators are near the top of the league for shot suppression, at the stingy end; the Flyers are one of the league’s worst, at the porous end. Expect that gap to show.
calls.call: The Senators allow fewer 5-on-5 shot attempts per 60 than the Flyers.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 4 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: On 5-on-5 shot attempts allowed per 60, Ottawa had 66.6 per 60 and Philadelphia 48.8 per 60. Coming in, Ottawa was at 52.7 per 60 and Philadelphia at 62.4 per 60.

OTT.head: We gave Ottawa a 68% chance, and Ottawa delivered.

PHI.head: We gave Philadelphia only a 32% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Philadelphia flipped the shot count
surprises.body: Philadelphia took 58% of the 5-on-5 shot attempts (adjusted for score and venue). From how these two usually play, Philadelphia would expect about 40%. A team strays this far about once every 125 games.
surprises.flipped: The Senators lock it down; the Flyers don’t

surprises.head: L. Ullmark stole one
surprises.body: L. Ullmark allowed 1 goal on shots worth 3.3 expected goals, 2.3 fewer than expected. Starting goalies had a night this good about once every 20 starts over the last three seasons.

story.head: Ullmark steals one
paras: Nick Cousins opened the scoring midway through the first. Carter Yakemchuk scored the winner midway through the third.
The Flyers had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Flyers win about seven in ten. Linus Ullmark made the difference in net, stopping 28 of 29.

items.text: The Flyers haven’t won in five.
One of the preview’s three calls held.
